decisions: SNAPSHOT AT ISSUE, NOT EFFECTIVE-DATED SALARY. A payslip is a DOCUMENT and must not change after it is handed over. Issuing freezes every figure and assigns a gap-free number via the counter-table pattern. An unissued month is a live preview at TODAY's salary and the register says so. Effective-dated salary stays deferred - one mechanism, three consumers, and half-building it inside a payslip feature would get it wrong for all three.

TWO BASES ON ONE SCREEN, DELIBERATELY. The payslip register is SETTLEMENT month (commission by paid_at, Riyadh). The review table below it is WORK month (what the driver earned from trips he drove, paid or not). The same driver legitimately shows two different totals - live, two July drivers do - so BOTH tables label their basis explicitly on screen. Left implied it reads as a bug in one of them.

paid_at, NOT period_label. period_label is a payout-RUN label, not the work period: live, one labelled 'Jul 2026' paid for work done entirely in June, another spanned two months, one driver had two payouts under one label (178+26, summed - taking 'the latest' would have dropped 26.00), and two locked zero trips. Attributing by trips would split one paid total across two documents.

THE COMMISSION BLOCK COMPOSES ON commission_payouts, NEVER RECOMPUTES. Where a payout settled in the month the block IS that payout by id; only where none exists does it fall back to accrual, and that fallback counts only trips with payout_id IS NULL - which is what stops one trip's commission reaching two payslips.

TERMINATED IS A LABEL RULE, NOT A GATE. Status priority: issued number, then Terminated, then No hire date, then month in progress, then Not issued. A terminated driver's final month is a legitimate payslip and stays issuable. A driver with NO HIRE DATE is shown but cannot be issued - enforced in the RPC with 23514, not just in the button.

0117 - THE SUGGESTED FIX WAS OVERRIDDEN WITH DATA. v_payroll_monthly billed NULL-hire people from 1900. Excluding them outright would have removed 4 of 5 drivers from July where they demonstrably worked, and an ACTIVE fleet_manager's 4,500/month from every month including August. The floor moved to COALESCE(hire_date, created_at::date) - a real date claiming only that nothing earlier is defensible. June payroll 36,000 -> 25,000; July and August unmoved; it degrades to nothing once real hire dates exist.

CHECK THE SET YOUR CLAIM IS ABOUT, NOT THE SET YOUR QUERY RETURNED. 0115's first draft claimed 'all 11 drivers have a hire date' - that 11 came from a query filtered to terminated_at is null and was written up as describing all 16. Five have none, all terminated, and the old coalesce would have allowed ten permanent 1,300 SAR documents for people who had left. Every verification block missed it because they inherited the wrong premise from the prose above them.

EVERY VIEW REPLACEMENT RESTATES ITS SECURITY FOOTER. create-or-replace does NOT preserve reloptions, so a replaced view silently reverts to owner-run and bypasses RLS on 68 tables while still returning rows. Now a standing lock in CLAUDE.md section 6, not a per-feature habit. Live: 40 views, 40 security_invoker, 0 anon-readable.
create-or-replace can only APPEND a column - never insert, reorder or rename (42P16, which cost 0112 an apply cycle).

A GUARD THAT WARNS AND CONTINUES IS WORSE THAN NO GUARD. The old stop-dev check printed 'STILL RUNNING - abort' and let the build run under a live dev server anyway, so the transcript read as protected. scripts/safe-build.sh now exits non-zero before touching .next.

THE PAYSLIPS SURFACE IS THE FIRST PLACE TWO PRINT SUBTREES COEXIST. Every other statement mounts alone, so 'one visible print id' was sufficient until now. Both ids are in all six globals.css rule groups and body.printing-review picks which survives - without it, printing either emits both.
noUnusedLocals + noUnusedParameters are ON. A parameter required by a signature gets an _ prefix; never delete it.
